title: Packers S Xavier McKinney: 'It really don't matter' who is at QB for Bucs
description: Packers safety Xavier McKinney: If we can't do our jobs, all 11, it don't matter who is at quarterback."
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers will not play against Baker Mayfield when they meet the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 4. Mayfield is set to miss multiple games after dislocating his thumb during the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss to the Vikings.

Instead, Green Bay will face Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie out of Kansas, who beat out Jake Browning to earn the backup job. You would think facing a quarterback who has yet to complete a pass in an NFL game sways things in the Packers' favor. Just don't tell that to safety and team captain Xavier McKinney.

"It really don't matter. If we can't do our jobs, all 11, it don't matter who is at quarterback," said McKinney on Monday. "Right now, everybody has to focus on doing their job, myself included."

The truth is, Green Bay can't take any opponent lightly, regardless of who is under center.

In Week 1, they allowed backup Carson Wentz to throw for three touchdowns and help erase a double-digit second-half deficit to lead Minnesota to victory. In Week 2, the Packers trailed by 10 points in the fourth quarter to a Jets team led by Geno Smith, who is now on his third team in three years.

Then, this past Thursday night, a sputtering Falcons team put up 35 points with a quarterback making his season debut. Michael Penix Jr. returned from a season-ending ACL injury to complete 72 percent of his passes for 256 yards and a touchdown.

Atlanta's offense leaned on running back Bijan Robinson, who rushed for 194 yards, one yard shy of his career high, and two touchdowns, though Penix was also highly effective.

Tampa Bay doesn't have a ball carrier of Robinson's caliber, but what they do have is a reason to run the ball and a quarterback who isn't afraid to scramble.

Daniels finished his college career with 1,445 yards on the ground and 23 rushing touchdowns. During the preseason, he totaled just 37 rushing yards in three appearances, but showed solid command of the Buccaneers offense, completing 27 of 44 passes for 239 yards, one passing touchdown, and no interceptions.

Green Bay needs a win on Sunday to avoid falling to 1-3. They will likely enter as the favorites, but that means very little when you haven't had a clean win over an opponent in nearly a year.

McKinney's teammates need to heed his words and come ready to play against a desperate Buccaneers team still searching for their first win.

title: This is the new tail section that Marco Bezzecchi debuted on the Aprilia
description: Bezzecchi tests new tail amid Aprilia's push in the title race against Ducati
fullText:
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi used his strong feel for development work to evaluate a new tail unit at the Red Bull Ring, taking responsibility for advancing the RS-GP's evolution alongside test rider Lorenzo Savadori. Jorge Martin will assess the new solution at a later stage in MotoGP.

Despite focus shifting on the new 850cc ruleset, Aprilia is still investing on its current RS-GP26. The Noale team wants to play all its cards in the championship fight against Ducati's Marc Marquez, with the team effort crucial to stopping the Spaniard's charge.

Martin remains at the top of the riders' standings, just 12 points ahead of reigning champion Marquez, while Bezzecchi is third on the other RS-GP, 42 points off the lead.

The Italian team is the only one with the ability to adapt its bike to the specific characteristics of individual circuits. Technical director Fabiano Sterlacchini is managing the group working on next year's 850cc Aprilia while development of the current MotoGP bike continues in parallel.

There is a strong sense of cohesion within Massimo Rivola's team, even though there is naturally rivalry between its two factory riders. At the Red Bull Ring, Aprilia introduced a new tail unit that was tested exclusively by Bezzecchi. The RS-GP of the Italian rider featured two additional flaps ahead of the supports holding its two-element rear wing.

The two curved profiles create a flow interaction with the rear-wing assembly and draw on concepts previously seen on Marquez's Ducati Desmosedici. The impression is that they help clean up the airflow around the tail unit, improving aerodynamic efficiency on the straights while providing a small increase in local downforce when the bike is leaned over.

Bezzecchi is regarded within Aprilia as an excellent development tester. He has developed a strong working relationship with test rider Savadori, and his sensitivity to evaluating new solutions has made him the Aprilia rider leading the development of the Noale manufacturer's ideas since last year, not only in terms of aerodynamics.

Martin, by contrast, was brought up with the philosophy of changing his bike as little as possible once he has found the right level of confidence. The Spaniard has complete faith in Bezzecchi's ability to develop the RS-GP, but prefers to wait for a later race before adopting solutions that his team-mate has already approved.

title: Mourinho’s preferred midfield double pivot at Real Madrid fails to deliver desired results so far
description: When Jose Mourinho was appointed the new head coach of Real Madrid, one of his biggest tasks was to bring back cohesion and understanding in the team.Mourinho’s biggest work required convincing Aure...
fullText:
When Jose Mourinho was appointed the new head coach of Real Madrid, one of his biggest tasks was to bring back cohesion and understanding in the team.

Mourinho's biggest work required convincing Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde to play together, after last season's dressing room debacle.

Mourinho left no stones unturned in trying to make the two players move on from the incident, and has even used them together in the double pivot on more than one occasion.

However, the Valverde-Tchouameni pairing has struggled to make an impact in the two matches they have started together, against Elche and Atletico Madrid.

Tchouameni Valverde duo has struggled to perform so far this season. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Against Elche, the duo played 86 minutes together and posted acceptable, if unspectacular, numbers.

The pair completed 78 passes between them, 25 of which came in the final third. However, neither featured among the team's top five for ball recoveries, and their combined involvement in plays was bettered by full-backs Marc Cucurella and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Their output in the derby was even more concerning. Valverde and Tchouameni managed just 55 passes between them across 71 minutes on the pitch together.

The one area they did excel in was ball recoveries, with Tchouameni making five and Valverde four in the derby.

Mourinho must find the right formula in midfield when the season restarts. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

The personal relationship between the two appears to have healed, with the duo embracing after Tchouameni's return from injury and Valverde applauding his teammate's introduction against Rayo Vallecano.

However, the wider concerns around stability and composure in the Real Madrid remains and the duo clearly hasn't been able to answer them.

Mourinho's coaching staff value Tchouameni as a figure who brings order and stability, yet the pairing has not provided the balance and progression Real Madrid require in the middle of the park.

Keeping that in mind, it will be interesting to see how Mourinho tries to find the right formula in midfield, when season resumes next month.

title: Strain making most of Bairns lifeline
description: Football has a funny way of making things fall into place - and Ryan Strain's signing feels like a case in point.  The Australia international's arrival raised a few eyebrows among the Bairns faithful earlier this summer.  It soon became clear Adams was injured and needed surgery, which explained the decision to bring in Strain.
fullText:
Football has a funny way of making things fall into place - and Ryan Strain's signing feels like a case in point.

The Australia international's arrival raised a few eyebrows among the Bairns faithful earlier this summer. That was no slight on Strain's ability.

We had already brought in Jack McMillan at right-back while Keelan Adams, a key performer in recent years, was also on the books.

It soon became clear Adams was injured and needed surgery, which explained the decision to bring in Strain. He had spent the first part of the summer at PFA Scotland's inaugural free agent training camp, but has since wasted little time making an impression at Falkirk.

Of the 17 players we brought in over the summer, Strain has arguably been the standout so far.

Others have impressed too, but the 29-year-old has slotted seamlessly into the right-back role and made it his own.

His influence seems to grow by the week. He's set up a goal in two of his past three outings, offers a threat with his set-piece delivery and has been reliable at the back, while his 14 tackles won is the joint highest in the Premiership.

Ironically, now that everyone is available again, it feels like his jersey to lose.

title: Juan Soto names the one player giving him confidence the Mets will contend next season
description: There is an awful lot that the New York Mets need to figure out during the offseason after a 2026 season to forget. The Mets have ended the season rock bottom of the NL East with a dismal 74-88 record on the year.
fullText:
There is an awful lot that the New York Mets need to figure out during the offseason after a 2026 season to forget.

The Mets have ended the season rock bottom of the NL East with a dismal 74-88 record on the year.

Having made decisions on the coaching staff already, the Mets can now turn their attention towards strengthening their roster for next year.

There has not been too much to shout about for Mets fans this season, but rookie Carson Benge has certainly provided some cause for optimism.

In his first season in the league, Benge hit 20 homers, 65 RBIs and totalled 168 hits, with an average of .282.

When asked why he's confident the Mets could compete next year, Soto replied: "Carson Benge."

"That's the confidence we have. We have a really good, talented, really young core that can help us. We just have to take them on the right path, show them where to go and how to go about this stuff, and play the game."

Benge is among the favourites for the Rookie of the Year award, but he faces strong competition from the likes of Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart.

"What he's been showing – not only his offensive side – it's more the defensive side, too. He's been showing it day in and day out, running the bases, stealing bags, and all that kinda stuff. He's a superstar. He's been doing a really good job," Soto added.

The only way is up for the Mets after they finished fifth in the NL East this season, but they have a lot to sort out if they are going to rival the Braves and the Phillies next year.

title: Fury vs Joshua: December Superfight Faces Fresh Trouble Before London Press Conference
description: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are due to meet in London on Wednesday as the build-up to their long-awaited heavyweight […]
fullText:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are due to meet in London on Wednesday as the build-up to their long-awaited heavyweight fight takes another tense turn. Fury vs Joshua is set for December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, but fresh disputes over promotion and anti-doping testing have raised questions about the event in recent days.

The fight has taken years to arrange, with venue talks, contract issues and promotional disagreements repeatedly delaying it. Saudi boxing figure Turki Alalshikh confirmed the Cardiff date last week after Joshua's team pushed for the fight to remain in the United Kingdom. Fury and Joshua will now appear together for the first time since the fight was formally confirmed, with the event expected to draw global attention.

The Fury vs Joshua fight is scheduled for December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff. The fight will stream globally on Netflix and is expected to begin in the early hours of December 12 in the United Kingdom to suit North American viewers.

Alalshikh confirmed the venue after months of discussions. Joshua's camp had pushed for a UK venue because of a clause in his contract. Promoters had previously considered Madison Square Garden and other U.S. locations.

The Fury vs Joshua fight will also feature the vacant WBA "super" heavyweight title, which Oleksandr Usyk vacated.

The Fury vs Joshua promotion faced another problem after Netflix and Ring Magazine materials listed Dana White as a co-promoter alongside Alalshikh's operation. Eddie Hearn, Joshua's long-time promoter, objected and said White's involvement conflicted with Joshua's agreement.

Hearn told Sky Sports there would be no press conference without his side being involved and said White would not attend.

Fury then questioned whether Joshua wanted the fight. He initially put the chances of the Fury vs Joshua bout happening at "one per cent" but later acknowledged that contracts had been signed and payments made.

"I do think it'll happen," Fury said. "Not unless they want to give the dough back."

Fury also said he expected to stop Joshua inside six or seven rounds and called him a "stepping stone" toward another fight with Usyk.

The Fury vs Joshua build-up also faced an anti-doping dispute. Joshua's team said both fighters were expected to enter the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association testing pool after signing their contracts.

Reports on Monday said Fury had not yet enrolled, creating uncertainty over whether Joshua would attend the London event. By Tuesday, reports from Ring Magazine's Mike Coppinger and Sky Sports indicated both fighters were traveling to London and the outstanding issues had been resolved enough for the press conference to go ahead. White is not expected to attend.

Fury and Joshua have known each other since sparring at Finchley Amateur Boxing Club in 2010. Their professional fight has since faced repeated delays over money, venues and promotional arrangements.

Fury, 38, returned from retirement earlier this year and stopped Mariusz Wach in July. Joshua, 36, stopped Jake Paul in December 2025 and then knocked out Kristian Prenga in July.

Together, Fury and Joshua have 66 wins, 52 knockouts and several world title reigns. Neither currently holds a major heavyweight belt. The December Fury vs Joshua fight remains one of boxing's biggest scheduled events, and Wednesday's London press conference will provide the next major update.

title: Fernando Alonso Confirms 2027 F1 Plans as New Contract Signed With Aston Martin
description: Aston Martin announces that Fernando Alonso will continue with the F1 team for another season in 2027, amid all talks of an exit. Since the start of the 2026 F1 season, Alonso has been in two minds about his future.…
fullText:
Aston Martin announces that Fernando Alonso will continue with the F1 team for another season in 2027, amid all talks of an exit.

Since the start of the 2026 F1 season, Alonso has been in two minds about his future. He set a timeline of summer break and since then it has been a dragging topic, even involving the FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem, publicly urging him to continue in the sport with Aston Martin.

However, Alonso has been adamant about his thought process, especially on the side of F1 regulations. While he says the performance of Aston Martin Honda is not the deciding factor, if the team would be in a better position in the standings, the Spaniard may have been clearer about it.

Nevertheless, Alonso has decided to continue on for another F1 season in 2027, with the announcement made ahead of this weekend's Bahrain GP in Malaysia. The team also took the opportunity to confirm Lance Stroll to remain as his teammate in the same pairing.

Having joined Aston Martin back in 2023, Alonso has had highs of podium finishes with the F1 team, but he is still looking for that 33rd race win and the third championship. The Spaniard has high hopes from Adrian Newey, who is spearheading the technical side, and the works deal with Honda.

"I'm very happy to sign a new contract with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team," said Alonso. "I took my time to make this decision, but racing is my life, my passion, and I know I still have the speed and determination to compete at the highest level. I'm committed for the long term with this team and to helping us succeed.

"I truly believe in what we are building: we have strong leadership, incredible people, partners and facilities. I look forward to making more memories on the racetrack in front of the passionate fans. Their energy creates an atmosphere that inspires me and is what makes our sport special."

A message from Fernando. pic.twitter.com/4qbPIoQRCe

— Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team (@AstonMartinF1) September 29, 2026

For Stroll, it was not surprising to continue at Aston Martin, being his father's F1 team. "I'm very happy to continue with Aston Martin Aramco for the long term," he said. "I've been on this journey since the beginning and I believe we have the resources and the people to become a winning team.

"There is so much hard work going on at Silverstone with real progress being made, and the determination I see in every department is a huge motivation for me. I know we are heading in the right direction, and my commitment is stronger than ever to help us achieve our goals."

Team boss Lawrence affirmed that both Alonso and Stroll are crucial to Aston Martin's journey to the top. "Lance and Fernando have been a crucial part of our journey, and we are very pleased to confirm that they will continue with us into the next chapter for the team." he said.

"Having two drivers with their level of experience, commitment and knowledge provides tremendous value to the whole organisation. We are here to win, and whilst our short-term focus remains on improving performance, I believe we have the world-class talent we need to achieve our long-term objectives."

title: Tebas says Man City should face 'most severe' sanctions if guilty of rule breaches
description: La Liga president Javier Tebas said Manchester City should face the "most severe sanction" available if they have breached financial regulations.And now it has been shown that UEFA was right about the sanctions it had imposed on Manchester City."
fullText:
La Liga president Javier Tebas said Manchester City should face the "most severe sanction" available if they have breached financial regulations.

Reports on Friday said an independent panel had found City guilty on all but one of 115 charges for breaking Premier League rules.

But no official announcement has been made by the English top-flight and there is, as yet, no indication of any potential punishment.

Abu Dhabi-backed City have always strenuously denied the charges and chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak issued a defiant statement on Saturday, underlining his conviction that City would be vindicated.

Potential sanctions could include a severe points deduction and possibly even expulsion from the Premier League, while other clubs are understood to be taking legal advice about possible compensation.

Tebas, in a lengthy social media post on Sunday, said that "equal rules for all" were essential to protect the integrity and sustainability the game.

The Spaniard, speaking at a football performance and health summit in London on Tuesday, said he had been raising concerns about City since 2017.

He said City, the dominant force in English football over the past decade, should now be severely punished.

"To have been breaking the rules for more than 10 years, however minor the breaches may have been, is very serious," he said.

"So there has to be a severe punishment for breaking the rules, not just to set an example, but because the rules were broken."

He added: "What has happened is very important, and hopefully it will be a before-and-after moment, not just in the Premier League but in European football as well, because the Manchester effect was an effect across all of Europe."

Tebas also called on the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reassess its decision to overturn a two-year European ban on City imposed by UEFA in 2020.

"In my opinion, the decisions of the CAS should be reviewed, because they lifted the sanction that UEFA had imposed on them (City)," he said.

"The sanctions were also lifted in a very questionable way. And now it has been shown that UEFA was right about the sanctions it had imposed on Manchester City."

City have been transformed under the ownership of Sheikh Mansour, whose Abu Dhabi United Group acquired the club in 2008.

They have won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League crown and multiple other trophies over the past 15 years.

title: The 3 most surprising teams of the college football season
description: The college football season is always full of surprises, and a few weeks into the season, it’s safe to say that a few teams have already delivered. There have already been a handful of teams that have simply not lived up to the hype, but there have been a few teams that have already defied…
fullText:
The college football season is always full of surprises, and a few weeks into the season, it's safe to say that a few teams have already delivered.

There have already been a handful of teams that have simply not lived up to the hype, but there have been a few teams that have already defied even the most optimistic of expectations.

While there's still a lot of season remaining, here are three teams that have gotten off to a surprising start to the 2026 season.

Two years ago, Mississippi State finished with just a 2-10 record, and things didn't get much better the following year, as the Bulldogs finished with just a 5-7 record. Through head coach Jeff Lebby's first two seasons, Mississippi State won just one SEC conference game. This year has already been radically different.

Through the first four weeks of the season, Mississippi State is 4-0 and 2-0 in the SEC after a gutty 31-24 comeback victory over No. 19 Missouri, and they're led by a legitimate Heisman Trophy candidate in Kamario Taylor, who has established himself as one of the best quarterbacks in the country through the first quarter of the regular season.

It's worth noting that Mississippi State did start the 2025 season with a 4-0 record, and those games included a win over No. 12 Arizona State. However, this team feels different in both its identity and talent. But we'll have a good idea of where they really stand next week when they host No. 7 Alabama.

The past two seasons have been rough for the Oklahoma State Cowboys as the team went a combined 4-20 in 2024 and 2025 and hadn't beaten an FBS team since September of 2024. After parting ways with Mike Gundy following last season, the Eric Morris era looked like more of the same in the season-opener as the Cowboys fell 24-10 to Tulsa to start the season.

Since then, however, Oklahoma State has looked like a totally new team, and that began with a stunning win over No. 6 Oregon just a week later. The Cowboys outplayed Oregon from almost start to finish, putting up 554 yards to beat Oregon 39-31, notching the program's first FBS win in two years.

Oklahoma State has kept the same momentum the past two weeks, shutting out Murray State 59-0 before blowing out previously unbeaten West Virginia 41-24 on the road, snapping an 18-game Big 12 losing streak that went all the way back to the 2023 season.

Heading into the season, Oklahoma State was expected to be one of the worst Power 4 teams in the country. Now, just four weeks into the season, the Cowboys are the No. 19 team in the AP Poll.

After firing head coach Bill Napier in the middle of what turned out to be a 4-8 season, the Florida Gators seemed to be headed toward a rebuilding year under new head coach Jon Sumrall. However, four games into the 2026 season, Sumrall has seemingly engineered an instant turnaround.

Florida went 3-0 to start the season, but the statement came this week against No. 4 Ole Miss. Florida rushed for 302 yards and six touchdowns in a 52-28 blowout. The 52 points tied the most Florida has ever scored against a top-five opponent in history with the only other time coming in the 1997 Sugar Bowl, when the Gators won the national championship. This came a week after Ole Miss established itself as a legitimate playoff contender with a win over LSU.

The biggest difference so far has been the offense. The Gators have scored at least 44 points in every game, and Sumrall is the first SEC head coach to score 200 points in his first four games. They've already scored 28 touchdowns, one shy of their total from all of last season.

The schedule doesn't get easier, with Missouri, Texas, and Georgia all coming in October. But after years of mediocrity in Gainesville, Florida suddenly looks like a real threat in the SEC and in the College Football Playoff race.

title: How much has ESPN changed since Stephen A. Smith joined the network?
description: T.Schneider/Depositphotos ESPN was already a major sports operation ESPN Inc. was already a large sports media operation when Stephen A. Smith joined in 2003 as an NBA Shootaround analyst. That year, the company also launched ESPN HD for high-definition television coverage.
fullText:
ESPN Inc. was already a large sports media operation when Stephen A. Smith joined in 2003 as an NBA Shootaround analyst. That year, the company also launched ESPN HD for high-definition television coverage.

Stephen A. Smith began at ESPN as an NBA studio analyst and later appeared on SportsCenter, ESPN News, First Take, and Pardon the Interruption. Those assignments gave him roles across several established programs.

Smith also hosted The Stephen A. Smith Show on ESPN Radio from 2005 through 2008. His early network work combined basketball analysis, general sports commentary, radio hosting, and recurring television appearances.

Stephen A. Smith received his own ESPN2 program in 2005 with Quite Frankly with Stephen A. Smith. The one-hour show featured sports news, commentary, and interviews before ending its run in 2007.

Quite Frankly gave Smith a dedicated television format before First Take became his signature ESPN role. His first tenure at the network ended in 2008, while his later return led to a larger morning presence.

Stephen A. Smith returned to ESPN programming in 2011 and joined First Take full-time in June 2012. The revised format featured Smith and Skip Bayless debating major sports topics at the desk.

First Take also introduced a new set, graphics, and format during that June relaunch. By September 2012, year-to-date viewership had risen 33%, while the third-quarter audience had increased 21% from the same period in 2011.

Stephen A. Smith became a central commentator on First Take as the program expanded its audience. By 2014, viewership among men ages 18 to 34 had increased for six consecutive years.

That same audience group grew 25% during 2014, while First Take became ESPN2's most-watched studio show. The figures established the debate program as a major part of ESPN's weekday schedule.

First Take expanded beyond linear television as digital viewing grew. In 2023, the program averaged 496,000 television viewers, setting its highest annual average at that point in the show's history.

First Take content also generated 250 million YouTube views during 2023, while its social accounts reached a combined 4.5 million followers. Those totals showed substantial consumption outside the television broadcast.

First Take set another annual audience record in 2025, averaging 517,000 viewers. The total increased 6% from 2024 and marked the program's most-watched calendar year through the end of 2025.

Other ESPN studio programs also grew that year. Get Up averaged 424,000 viewers, while NFL Live posted its strongest annual performance since 2016, showing that audience gains extended beyond First Take.

Stephen A. Smith signed a new multi-year ESPN agreement in March 2025 that keeps him with the company for at least five more years. The deal also covers appearances across additional ESPN programming.

Smith remains First Take's featured commentator and executive producer. He also co-executive produces the program through Mr. SAS Productions, alongside ESPN and Omaha Productions, which gives him responsibilities beyond appearing on camera.

ESPN expanded into subscription streaming with ESPN+ in April 2018. The paid service launched inside the ESPN App and added thousands of live events, original programming, and on-demand sports content.

That transition advanced on August 21, 2025, when ESPN launched a direct subscription service carrying its full network lineup. Fans gained access to those channels without needing a traditional television package.

ESPN's expanded direct subscription service launched an Unlimited plan at $29.99 per month. The package provided access to ESPN networks and services, covering about 47,000 live events at launch.

The enhanced ESPN App also introduced multiview options, integrated game statistics, fantasy features, and personalized SportsCenter content. Those additions combine live viewing, information, and account features into one digital platform.

Fun fact: Before becoming ESPN's loudest debate fixture, Stephen A. Smith attended college on a basketball scholarship and played for legendary coach Clarence "Big House" Gaines.

Juan Alejandro Bernal R/Deopsitphotos

ESPN added Monday Night Football to its cable schedule in 2006 after the franchise moved from ABC. The change placed one of the NFL's longest-running prime-time packages directly on ESPN each week.

The 2024 Monday Night Football season averaged 15 million viewers per game and reached 112 million people. Those figures show the continuing scale of NFL programming within ESPN's broader television and streaming business.

ESPN and Disney secured new 11-year NBA and WNBA media agreements. The NBA agreement began with the 2025 to 2026 season, while the WNBA agreement started with its 2026 season.

The agreements run through the 2035-2036 NBA season and the 2036 WNBA season. ABC remains the exclusive NBA Finals television home, while ESPN distributes basketball coverage across television and streaming platforms.

"I wouldn't be surprised," Clark predicts that overseas WNBA games next year offer added context on how her influence may extend beyond domestic competition as the league considers broader international opportunities.

ESPN has expanded from a cable-centered sports network into a business spanning television, streaming, digital products, and audio since Stephen A. Smith first joined the company as an NBA analyst in 2003.

Smith's career followed that broader shift from studio analyst to featured commentator and executive producer. ESPN also added direct subscriptions, richer digital tools, and expanded rights packages as sports viewing habits changed.

title: Tuchel makes one change to England squad for Czechia clash
description: Thomas Tuchel has replaced Nico O’Reilly with Rio Ngumoha in England’s squad to face Czechia in Tuesday’s UEFA Nations League match at Fortuna Arena, according to the Mirror.O’Reilly missed Mo...
fullText:
Thomas Tuchel has replaced Nico O'Reilly with Rio Ngumoha in England's squad to face Czechia in Tuesday's UEFA Nations League match at Fortuna Arena, according to the Mirror.

O'Reilly missed Monday's training due to injury and has not recovered in time to make the trip to Prague.

Lewis Hall and Myles Lewis-Skelly are options to replace the Manchester City youngster in the starting line-up.

Ngumoha was left out for the Three Lions' defeat to Spain. He is now in line to make his senior competitive debut after making his bow in June's friendly win over New Zealand.

Tuchel rates the 18-year-old highly, with the England boss 'very excited about his potential and about his natural courage and adventurous style of play.'

The Liverpool youngster is unlikely to start against Czechia with Anthony Gordon, Morgan Rogers, Eberechi Eze and Morgan Gibbs-White ahead of him for the wide attacking positions.

Ngumoha will be hoping to get a chance as he seeks to break into England's starting XI before the 2028 European Championship.

Meanwhile, Ezri Konsa has shaken off his fitness concerns to make the trip to Czechia, having missed Monday's training.

The Arsenal centre-back has been a regular under Tuchel, featuring in every game at the World Cup and in the defeat to Spain.

England are aiming to avoid another slow start to their Nations League campaign and will look to secure a victory at Czechia.

They will next travel to Croatia this Saturday before hosting Czechia at Wembley next Tuesday.

title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 4
description: Nick’s NFL power rankings heading into Week 4
fullText:
Somehow, the Buffalo Bills turned the football over five times and still WON THE GAME! Of course, it was against the Chargers, who are currently — and historically — allergic to winning, but James Cook's 154 yards on the ground helped give Buffalo the 24-16 win, and they remain at the top of the standings here.

Brock Purdy and the 49ers are one of the hottest teams in football. Purdy went for 297 yards and four touchdowns against an inferior Cardinals team, who pushed the 49ers in the 36-30 game. Still, through all the injuries, the 49ers remain a top team in the NFL.

The Chiefs went into Miami and easily handled the Dolphins. Patrick Mahomes was efficient (20 of 24 for 246 yards with two touchdowns), and Rashee Rice finally got going with seven catches for 88 yards. Miami offered little resistance in the 24-10 win, and the Chiefs are one of the four undefeated teams that remain in the NFL.

Seattle goy Sam Darnold back from his hip injury, but Washington did an excellent job harrassing the Seahawks all game. Darnold finished with 379 passing yards and four touchdowns, but Marcus Mariota did enough to give the Commanders a 33-31 home victory.

The Rams drop to 1-2 but remain in the top five. Massive credit to the Broncos, who appeared dead for much of the game but battled back with 30 second-half points. Matt Stafford finished with 390 yards passing and two touchdowns, but the Rams' game plan shifted after a Terrance Ferguson injury, and they were without Puka Nukua, who they hope will return soon.

Tyler Loop! The Ravens and Dallas were headed to overtime after Dak Prescott led the Cowboys down the field on a last-minute drive to tie the game with a field goal. Unfortunately for Dallas, Lamar Jackson found Zay Flowers for 27 yards, which set up a 56-yarder from Loop for a big road victory over Jerry Jones' Cowboys.

The Vikings have moved eight spots up in the rankings over the last two weeks. They're undefeated, but sit seventh in the rankings; this is because of my discomfort with Kyler Murray, who missed Week 2 with a concussion. The Vikings' defense, led by Brian Flores, is playing amazing football, and they beat up on the Buccaneers, 23-16. Still, the offense isn't going to be bailed out by the strong defense every week; the team must become more complementary.

The Broncos defeated a very good Rams team at home with second-half resilience. The win was similar to their win over the Giants last year, where they scored 30 points in the fourth quarter; they did that in the second half, and the Broncos' defense slowed down Matt Stafford when it mattered most.

Chicago dismantled the Philadelphia Eagles with 38-year -old journeyman quarterback Case Keenum. Ben Johnson continues to prove why he's an offensive wizard, and he unlocked the potential of Luther Burden III in the game. Kalif Raymond finished with six grabs for 90 yards and a touchdown, as Philadelphia was held to seven points and 248 total yards. Impressive win against a struggling, now 2-1 Eagles team.

The Bengals gave up 292 yards and three touchdowns to Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. After two strong weeks of defensive football, the Bengals' defense struggled to stop Ja'Marr Chase (9 catches for 98 yards and a touchdown) and Jaylen Warren, who rushed for 127 yards. Cincinnati will be okay, but this was a tough loss.

The New England Patriots are spiraling right now, and Jacksonville took advantage of that fact in Week 3. Jacksonville beat up on the Patriots, 35-6, with Drake Maye looking very bad, finishing 14 of 25 for 199 yards with a pair of interceptions. Jacksonville got back on track against the AFC champs from last season.

Detroit was pushed by the New York Jets, but they found a way to win late in the 31-24 game against a feisty Jets team. Jaymeir Gibbs finished with 99 yards and a pair of touchdowns on 20 carries, and the Lions sit at 2-1.

The Eagles are a 2-1 team that does not inspire much hope. Jalen Hurts still has his flaws as a passer, and they were just embarrassed in primetime by the Chicago Bears. Things do not get much easier for the Eagles, as they host the Rams next Sunday and then travel to London to play the Jaguars.

The Raiders are undefeated! And they just went into a hostile New Orleans environment and defeated the Saints 35-21. Brock Bowers' return was exciting, as the young tight end caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. Kirk Cousins is doing enough to put the Raiders into advantageous situations, as they sit undefeated.

I hate having the 1-2 Dallas Cowboys this high, especially with their suspect defense through three weeks. But I know how explosive their offense can be with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Plus, their rushing attack is getting going, and they'll be getting Tyler Smith back soon. The defense remains an issue, of course, but Dallas stays put at 14.

I didn't expect to see Aaron Rodgers dial back the clock against a Bengals defense that tormented the Buccaneers and Texans in their first two matchups. The Steelers' defense remains their strength, but competent quarterback play makes them a threat, so they are in the top-fifteen.

The Colts finally got their first victory against the Houston Texans on a last-second field goal. Indianapolis struggled to do much against a very good Texans defense, but they found a way to get a valuable win and send the Texans to 0-3.

I don't like having the 0-3 Texans this high, but I feel better about their position — specifically with their defense — than I do with the remaining teams, including the injured Giants, so here we are. Houston pushed Buffalo and the Colts to near victories; they must get more out of their offense and learn to secure wins, but they're better than their 0-3 record would indicate.

The Giants are 2-1 and handled their business in a sloppy noreaster against the Tennessee Titans. New York has issues with Jameis Winston; the trade for J.J. McCarthy may eventually solve that problem, but the Giants are beat up on both sides of the ball. However, Jordan Stout is a stud. The Giants can still compete for this NFC East with their current injury situation, and I expect better play out of Jameis Winston, although I'm relieved they'll have another viable option.

Washington pulled off one of the season's more impressive wins, defeating the Super Bowl champions 33-31 at home. Perhaps it was Sam Darnold jitters, or the dreaded one-o-clock start for a West Coast team — I'm not sure — but it does seem like Washington's defense has improved, and Marcus Mariota did enough against Mike Macdonald's talented defense

Las Vegas just might be a much better football team than many anticipated, and the Saints found that out firsthand. Tyler Shough played well, throwing four touchdowns with 255 yards passing. Still, the Raiders forced four turnovers and the Saints lost running back Travis Etienne to injury. New Orleans is a quality 1-2 team, but they're still young and learning themselves.

The Panthers suffered a tough loss to the now 2-1 Browns. Bryce Young threw for 291 yards and one touchdown in the 21-18 loss, but the Dawg Pound did enough to earn DeShaun Watson his first home win in years.

The New York Jets are the SECOND-rated team in the NFC East. They've lost their last two, but were in both games and have looked competent on offense with Geno Smith. They're exceeding expectations and have been solid defensively. The Jets are no longer a doormat in the NFL.

Look, the Browns are 2-1. Watson finished with 144 passing yards and a pair of passing touchdowns in a slow-paced win against the Panthers. I don't think the Browns are a legitimate contender in the AFC North, but they beat two NFC South teams and have looked better than I expected, which is something.

The Falcons just beat up on the Green Bay Packers in Wisconsin, 35-14. Green Bay rushed for 17 yards at home as favorites on Thursday Night Football — great job by Atlanta's defense. The return of Michael Penix proved to be just what Atlanta needed. We'll see if they can continue to stack wins with help from talented play-makers like Bijan Robinson and Drake London.

Arizona pushed San Francisco in the 30-36 loss. They leaned on Jeremiyah Love, who had 21 carries for 90 yards, while Jacoby Brissett tossed 52 passes for 280 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The Cardinals are better than expected, but are still a team that could use an upgrade in personnel.

Yes — what a fall for the Patriots! There is no more excusing it — THEYYYYY STINK! New England is all sorts of messed up on offense, and Drake Maye has looked lost through three games. Their offensive line is injured and hasn't played well and no receivers can create separation. It's a tough watch for the defending Super Bowl champions.

The Packers were embarrassed at home against the Falcons. Green Bay, much like the Patriots and the next team we'll discuss, looked lost offensively, and Jordan Love is the only reason they have not imploded. They can't run the ball at all, and their offense is completely one-dimensional.

Only the Chargers can lose a game when their opponent turns the ball over five times. Justin Herbert's late interception was terrible and this offense is playing horribly. Omarion Hampton doesn't appear to be a fit for Mike McDaniel's scheme, which has looked bad with this personnel. It's full-on panic in Los Angeles for the Chargers.

The Buccaneers are winless, and Baker Mayfield just suffered a hand injury. They, at least, weren't embarrassed against the Vikings, but still picked up the L.

Tennessee lost to the Giants in a monsoon. Cam Ward struggled, but the Titans' defense was solid against Jameis Winston and the Giants' heavy rushing attack. The Titans are young, but have been competitive in their last two games. Still, they're a bottom team in the NFL.

Miami lost to the Kansas City Chiefs and De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL. Again, it's going to be a very long year for the Dolphins.

title: Former Braves Closer, 2-Time All-Star And MLB Saves Leader Ends Career With 3 Words
description: The Atlanta Braves got a retirement update from a former star who suddenly announced the end of his career on the last day of the season.
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves are preparing for another postseason run with one of their most important bullpen reinforcements finally nearing full strength.

Robert Suarez, who missed several months with an elbow injury, has returned to action at a crucial time as Atlanta prepares to face the rival Philadelphia Phillies in the Wild Card round.

"The Braves bullpen was one of the best in baseball even without set-up man Robert Suarez for three months," Jesus Cano reported for The Athletic. "But they were glad to see him make two appearances since returning from right elbow inflammation this past week."

Suarez's return gives Atlanta another high-leverage option alongside Raisel Iglesias and the rest of a deep relief corps. He posted a 0.56 ERA across his first 31 appearances before his elbow issue sidelined him in June.

But alongside the news of Suarez's imminent return, the Braves also received an update on a former centerpiece of their bullpen at the end of the regular season. Kirby Yates, who spent the 2022 and 2023 seasons in Atlanta, announced that his playing career is officially over.

Cubs Castoff Cut By New Team Immediately After Disastrous Outing

Yates confirmed his retirement decision publicly after making the first start of his 12-year MLB career for the Pittsburgh Pirates on Saturday, pitching one and two-thirds scoreless innings against the Detroit Tigers. The appearance was also part of a memorable final day for Justin Verlander, who was making his final MLB appearance for Detroit.

"This is it," Yates announced in a postgame interview with SportsNet Pittsburgh. "I just didn't really want to say anything, publicly, until the end."

That three-word message delivered a clear answer after Yates hinted at the idea of ending his career leading up to the final appearance.

Yates leaves baseball as a two-time All-Star and the 2019 National League saves leader. That season with the San Diego Padres produced 41 saves and a 1.19 ERA, establishing the right-hander as one of baseball's premier closers. He later earned his second All-Star selection with the Texas Rangers in 2024 after recording 33 saves and a 1.17 ERA.

Yankees Legend Quickly Deletes Jab At CC Sabathia Monument Park Decision

Yates originally joined the Braves on a two-year, $8.25 million contract before the 2022 season. His first year in Atlanta followed an extended recovery from elbow surgery, but he returned to become a reliable bullpen piece and posted a 3.28 ERA across 60 and one-third innings in 2023.

His career ultimately included stops with eight MLB organizations, 518 appearances, 101 saves and a 3.35 ERA. He also overcame the unusual path of reaching the majors after going undrafted out of junior college.

"I don't have anything left, let's put it that way," Yates told SportsNet Pittsburgh. "I've been running on fumes here for a while… I've given this game everything I have and in return it's given me more than I could ever thank it for or imagine."

For many Braves fans, Yates' retirement announcement will recall some big moments in the recent past, including his only postseason appearance, which came in the 2023 National League Division Series against the Phillies. As the Braves once again prepare to face their division rival in the playoffs, fans will take a moment to remember the former bullpen piece as a long and successful career comes to an end.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Bayern Munich leader surprised by Florian Wirtz struggles at Liverpool
description: The FC Bayern legend did not foresee these struggle for Florian Wirtz at Liverpool.
fullText:
Bayern Munich supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has been sounding off on many topics of late.

Abendzeitung's Maximilian Koch asked if he could see Bayern Munich taking another run at struggling Germany international and Liverpool attacker Florian Wirtz at some point in the future, Rummenigge recused himself from that kind of decision.

"First of all, that's not my job. It's a matter for the board. And we mustn't forget that Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry play in that position, and there are other options as well, such as Ismael Saibari. There's no need to spend the kind of money that Wirtz would probably cost to sign a fourth player for that position. That's why I say — before making any move, a player needs to think very carefully about it," Rummenigge said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia).

However, Rummenigge did indicate that you never know what the future might hold.

"Whether something might still be possible at some point? I don't know. The question is whether Wirtz is happy at Liverpool. I can't judge that. Uli and I were in contact with his father and mother for a while. Then they decided to take a different path, and we respected that," Rummenigge stated.

When asked if he was surprised that Wirtz was still struggling at Liverpool, Rummenigge admitted that it was a bit shocking to see the former Bayer Leverkusen star still scuffling.

"To be honest, yes. We were given the impression that he chose Liverpool because the manager back then, Arne Slot, had promised him the #10 position — the role he had also played at Leverkusen. That was an important factor in his decision to join Liverpool. There were no big differences financially. He made his decision, and we accepted it," said Rummenigge.

title: Maple Leafs blockbuster Marchenko trade is exactly what Auston Matthews needed
description: The Maple Leafs trade a day before the season begins is exactly what the captain needed.
fullText:
A big trade happened in the NHL on Monday, and this blockbuster deal helps the Toronto Maple Leafs in plenty of ways. The trade came out of nowhere, and the Maple Leafs continue building a solid group heading into the season.

TRADE: We've acquired forwards Kirill Marchenko, Miles Wood, and goaltender Elvis Merzļikins from the Columbus Blue Jackets— Toronto Maple Leafs (@MapleLeafs) September 28, 2026

MORE: NHL player comments on why American players want out of Canada

Jan 31, 2026; Vancouver, British Columbia, CAN; Toronto Maple Leafs forward Auston Matthews (34) celebrates his game winning shootout goal against the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Maple Leafs need more playmakers to help Auston Matthews' production, and this move certainly does that. The money is more, but the player in Kirill Marchenko is better than Matthew Knies. Knies brings more physicality to his game and plays with an edge; Marchenko is the player that they need to pair with Matthews.

The Leafs have now made multiple moves to improve their offense, and their top six is looking very strong heading into this season. They may go from drafting Gavin McKenna at number one to competing for a playoff spot and making some noise in the Eastern Conference.

The trade doesn't make sense at first with them trading a young player with less of a cap hit, but the Leafs want more offense and play drivers, which Marchenko is very good at.

Mar 2, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Columbus Blue Jackets right wing Kirill Marchenko (86) plays the puck against the New York Rangers during the third period at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The key to Marchenko's ability is his drive and playmaking ability. He registered 67 points in 76 games with a roster that is far less talented than the Leafs. Now, he joins a revamped team that has numerous playmakers, and let's not forget what Auston Matthews can be when he has the puck on his stick.

This power play is going to be very fun to watch from another angle of this trade. Last year, they were the 15th-best unit, and that is even with an absent Auston Matthews. Marchenko will help with setting up his teammates, creating opportunities for this team to score more goals and improve their offense.

This trade is a win for the Leafs, and this top six forward core looks very good on paper. We will see how the team plays this season, but the team should have lots to cheer for as they acquired a very good player. It will be interesting to see how their new coach shapes up the offense, but Jim Hiller has plenty to work with and can help the Leafs get back to the playoffs.

title: Bears’ quarterback plan for Jets remains unsettled despite Case Keenum’s big night
description: Case Keenum threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns and scored on a goal-line sneak in the Chicago Bears’ 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, his first NFL start since Dec. 24, 2023. Ben Johnson still would not commit to him for Sunday. Caleb Williams is highly unlikely to be back from […] The post Bears’ quarterback plan for Jets remains unsettled despite Case Keenum’s big night appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Case Keenum threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns and scored on a goal-line sneak in the Chicago Bears' 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, his first NFL start since Dec. 24, 2023. Ben Johnson still would not commit to him for Sunday.

Caleb Williams is highly unlikely to be back from a Grade 2 hamstring strain when the New York Jets visit Soldier Field on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. That leaves Johnson choosing between Keenum and Tyson Bagent on a six-day turnaround.

"We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff and we'll see where we need to go from here," Johnson said. "There was a reason why Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."

That seems to lean toward Bagent, who finished camp ahead of Keenum, the Bears' third-stringer when the season opened. Keenum's night makes the call harder than it looked a week ago. He completed 24 of 34 passes for a 110.8 passer rating, and Chicago's defense forced three takeaways and held Philadelphia to seven points in a win that moved the Bears to sixth in Sports Fountain's Week 3 top 10.

Johnson used a similar line on Saturday, the Chicago Sun-Times noted, and later said he was fairly set on starting Keenum by that point. Johnson has also described the Eagles call as an easy one, citing how convincing Keenum was in practice. Treating Monday's answer as a decision would ignore how he handled the same question two days before kickoff.

Ben Johnson when asked who will start next week at QB:

There is a reason Tyson ended training camp as our number 2 QB.

Obviously nothing concrete but from the sounds of that seems like Tyson will be the starter next week. #Bears #DaBears pic.twitter.com/BO4cGndupm

— Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) September 29, 2026

Bagent entered the concussion protocol after playing the final two drives of the Week 2 loss to Minnesota, missed the first two practices of the week and was not cleared until Sunday morning. Keenum took the starting reps and the game plan was built around him. Bagent is healthy this week, so the preparation problem that decided Monday's start has gone away.

Bagent is 2-2 as a starter, with all four of those games coming as an undrafted rookie in 2023. Keenum, 38, had gone 1,009 days without a start, and his main job over the last two seasons was mentoring Williams and Bagent. He also had help, as Philadelphia opened the second half with three straight three-and-outs and gained seven yards on those nine plays.

Williams was hurt on Sept. 20, and the three-to-four-week estimate on his strain points to a return somewhere between the Oct. 11 trip to Green Bay and the Oct. 18 game in Atlanta. Whoever starts against the Jets may only be holding the job for one or two weeks.

title: ESPN predicts final score of FSU vs. Virginia in Week 5
description: Mike Norvell and the FSU Seminoles are hosting Virginia. Here is what ESPN's analytics indicate about the game.
fullText:
The FSU Seminoles are gearing up for their second ACC game of the season, with the Virginia Cavaliers coming to Tallahassee. Florida State is looking to build on their 34-7 win over the Central Arkansas Bears, which got them to 2-2 on the season.

The Cavaliers (3-1) will be a difficult test for the Seminoles and are coming off a 42-3 win over the Delaware Blue Hens. All three of their wins have come at home, with their loss coming in a neutral-site game against the West Virginia Mountaineers.

Ahead of FSU-Virginia, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his SP+ metrics. Connelly has Virginia picking up a 30-24 victory, handing FSU its third loss against a Power Four opponent. His metrics give Virginia a 65% chance of winning and have them covering the spread after they opened as slight favorites.

FSU is the No. 53 team in the SP+ team rankings after Week 4. They have an overall rating of 57.8, with a 58.2 rating on offense and a 0.4 rating on defense. Virginia is the No. 21 team and features a 66.5 overall rating. They have a 58.4 offensive rating and a -7.9 defensive rating.

The game between FSU and Virginia starts at 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday in Doak Campbell Stadium. The game will be on ESPN2, with Jay Alter as the play-by-play announcer, Tom Luginbill as the color commentator, and Lauren Sisler as the sideline reporter.

title: U20 Elite League: Köln winger Mikey Moore scores again as Spurs loanee shines for England U20
description: England U20 maintained their perfect start in the U20 Elite League with a comfortable victory over their French counterpart. Mikey Moore, who scored on his debut against Italy, added another goal to h...
fullText:
England U20 maintained their perfect start in the U20 Elite League with a comfortable victory over their French counterpart. Mikey Moore, who scored on his debut against Italy, added another goal to his collection in the fast start for Darren Moore's side.

Shumaira Mheuka put England ahead with the sweeper goalkeeper Ollie Whatmuff providing the perfect assist before Moore doubled their advantage after a decent finish from the left flank inside the first 20 minutes. While Köln's winger captained England, Wolfsburg defender Mathys Angely wore the armband for France.

Axel Tape, who is playing for Spanish side Levante on loan from Bayer Leverkusen, took over that responsibility after the break as coaches could make more than five substitutions in the U20 Elite League.

France halved the deficit in a heated second-half encounter as Angers forward Prosper Peter won and converted a penalty-kick. The World Cup semi-finalists lost both of their first games in this competition against Germany and England.

England U20 have highly-rated talents from some of the biggest Premier League clubs, including Liverpool's midfielder Trey Nyoni, Everton's fan favorite Harrison Armstrong and Manchester United's Ayden Heaven and Shea Lacey.

They will end the international break with a game against Germany on October 3rd. Hannes Wolf's side will play against Italy U20 later on Tuesday.

title: Did Notre Dame make the right move with Ohio State WR transfers?
description: Notre Dame took two Ohio State wide receivers in its 2026 transfer class. Was it the right move for the Irish?
fullText:
Now that we are four games in the 2026, it's pretty easy to see which transfer players have made impacts for Notre Dame, but a pair of herald receivers aren't included in that group.

The Irish brought in a pair of Ohio State wide receivers during the cycle in Mylan Graham and Quincy Porter. Both of them were considered 5-star prospects coming out of high school, and Graham is from Fort Wayne. At the time it made perfect sense, with how well the Buckeyes have done producing elite talent at the position, grabbing a few of their players who weren't seeing the field seemed like a perfect marriage with Notre Dame.

Unfortunately, it hasn't worked out for the Irish. Graham has been healthy, but hasn't been as impactful as was expected. On the year he has just three catches for 32 yards without a score. Not the production that anyone expected.

As for Porter, the New Jersey native came from a familiar school to Notre Dame, Bergen Catholic. It hasn't been a production issue for him, he just hasn't been able to see the field. Porter, on Monday, was ruled out for the remainder of the year with another knee surgery, one that has been bothering him since the spring.

It was hard to image these two having a minimal impact for the Irish, but here we are. Notre Dame was very selective in taking transfer this cycle, as the hit rate has dropped. Defensive tackles Tionne Gray and Francis Brewu have been a great additions, so have nickels Jayden Sanders and DJ McKinney.

Like recruiting, not all players pan out. Fortunately for Notre Dame, there's plenty of time for Graham and Porter to turn around their careers in South Bend. They just won't be immediate impact transfers like some of their classmates.

title: Bayern boss breaks silence on Florian Wirtz transfer links amid Liverpool struggles
description: Bayern Munich made a strong push to sign Florian Wirtz in the summer of 2025, but the attacking midfielder ultimately opted to join Liverpool from Bayer Leverkusen instead.With Wirtz having since come...
fullText:
Bayern Munich made a strong push to sign Florian Wirtz in the summer of 2025, but the attacking midfielder ultimately opted to join Liverpool from Bayer Leverkusen instead.

With Wirtz having since come under a lot of criticism for failing to live up to expectations at Liverpool, speculation has arisen that Bayern could reignite their interest in the German star.

However, based on comments from FC Bayern supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, a move for the 23-year-old doesn't seem particularly likely.

"First of all, that's not my job," Rummenigge told AZ when asked about the possibility of Bayern reigniting their interest in Wirtz, pointing out that it is the responsibility of the club's sporting management.

"You mustn't forget that Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry play in that position, and there are other options such as Ismael Saibari. There's no need to buy a fourth player for the amount of money Wirtz would probably cost.

"That's why I say: every step a player takes is something he has to think through carefully beforehand."

Rummenigge admits that he's surprised Wirtz has struggled so much at Liverpool.

"Honestly: yes. We were given the impression that he was going to Liverpool because the manager at the time, Arne Slot, had promised him the No. 10 position, which he had also played at Leverkusen.

"That was an important factor in his decision to choose Liverpool. Financially, there were no dramatic differences. He made his decision, and we accepted it."

The 71-year-old doesn't completely want to shut the door to Wirtz, though.

"Whether something else could still be possible at some point? I don't know," the supervisory board member said.

"The question is whether Wirtz is happy at Liverpool. I can't judge that. Uli [Hoeneß] and I were in contact with his father and mother for a while. Then they made a different decision, and we respected that."

title: Three ways Colorado football can upset No. 10 Texas Tech
description: Colorado hosts unbeaten No. 10 Texas Tech on Saturday. Here are three ways the Buffaloes can clean up their offense and pull off the upset.
fullText:
Colorado football will return to Folsom Field on Saturday with two straight losses and a difficult assignment against No. 12 Texas Tech. The Red Raiders are 4-0 and opened as a near two-touchdown road favorite.

Colorado has enough talent to make the game uncomfortable for Texas Tech, yet it will need cleaner work from an offense that has scored only 20 points in its last two games. The Buffaloes also need to settle their quarterback plan after they replaced Julian Lewis with Isaac Wilson during the Baylor loss.

Here are the clearest ways Colorado might be able to pull off an upset vs. the Red Raiders.

Colorado needs a clear direction at quarterback throughout the week. Wilson led a 95-yard touchdown drive at Baylor and completed a 17-yard scoring pass to Williams after entering at halftime.

Lewis remains a talented young passer, but the offense has struggled to find rhythm across the past two games. A full week of first-team preparation for one quarterback would give Brennan Marion a chance to tailor the plan and avoid another midgame change.

Joseph Williams has become Colorado's most dependable offensive weapon, leading the team with 361 yards and three touchdowns. He set career highs at Baylor with 11 catches for 127 yards and a touchdown.

Quanell Farrakhan Jr. added seven catches for 117 yards in Waco, showing Colorado can still generate production despite injuries to Danny Scudero Jr. and DeAndre Moore Jr. Kam Perry and Ernest Campbell give the offense more options if the staff builds the game plan around quick throws, intermediate routes and shots downfield.

Texas Tech's backfield is the starting point. J'Koby Williams has 285 yards and three touchdowns, while Cameron Dickey has 227 yards and four scores. The pair has combined for 512 rushing yards and seven touchdowns through four games.

Colorado linebackers will be without Tyler Martinez after his foot injury at Baylor. Liona Lefau, Gideon Lampron and the rest of the room must handle the workload against a Texas Tech offense that uses quarterback Thomas Castellanos in a wildcat package near the goal line and has already rushed for two touchdowns.

Colorado's upset path starts with a strong showing from the secondary and linebackers and by giving the receivers a chance in a game with almost no margin for error.

title: Caitlin Clark’s playoff milestone offers the Fever one bright spot before must-win Game 2
description: Indiana lost Game 1 by 17 points, but Caitlin Clark still reached a postseason mark that shows how much the Fever rely on her to create offense.
fullText:
Caitlin Clark's playoff milestone offers the Fever one bright spot before must-win Game 2 originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Indiana Fever had little reason to celebrate after Sunday's 102-85 loss to the Las Vegas Aces. A'ja Wilson scored 38 points, the Aces shot 59.4 percent from the field, and Indiana left Las Vegas one defeat from elimination.

Caitlin Clark still gave the Fever something to carry into Game 2. She finished with 15 points and 10 assists, with the assists ranking second in a postseason game in franchise history, according to an Indiana team announcement reported by Athlon Sports.

It was a milestone hidden inside a difficult night. Clark shot 6-of-17 from the floor and committed six turnovers, but she also created scoring chances while Las Vegas repeatedly made Indiana work for clean looks.

An assist total can make an offense look healthier than it felt. Clark found teammates often enough to reach double figures, yet the Fever never found a sustained answer for the Aces' defense or their own mistakes.

Indiana committed 16 turnovers. Las Vegas turned those giveaways into 28 points, a number coach Stephanie White singled out after the game. Those possessions prevented the Fever from building momentum and gave the Aces opportunities before Indiana's defense could get set.

Aliyah Boston scored a team-high 18 points, while Kelsey Mitchell went 4-of-16 for 12. Clark and Mitchell have powered the Fever's backcourt all season, but Indiana needs both players to find a better rhythm when the series moves home.

The milestone matters because it shows Clark can still create for others against an elite opponent. The concern is how hard the Aces made every possession around those assists.

MORE: Dream give Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard a moment to celebrate before playoff win

Game 2 is Tuesday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The best-of-three series ends if Las Vegas wins again, leaving the Fever with no time to treat Sunday as a learning experience.

Clark does not need to chase another record. Indiana needs her passing to lead to easier shots, fewer rushed possessions and a more balanced attack. Boston's interior scoring gives the Fever one option; Mitchell's shooting could give them another if she finds space.

The Aces have already shown what happens when Indiana's offense stalls. Clark's 10 assists are impressive. Turning that playmaking into a win is the challenge waiting at home.

title: Barcelona hit by injury scare as Raphinha taken off at half-time of Brazil friendly
description: The worst possible news.
fullText:
Barcelona star Raphinha started Tuesday's friendly clash with Australia for Brazil but was taken off at half-time with a potential injury.

The CBF said in a statement: "Suffering from discomfort in his right thigh, striker Raphinha was substituted at halftime."

There are no further details available just yet but the sight of Raphinha going off, particularly with his history of hamstring problems, will be the last thing Barcelona wanted to see during this international break.

Raphinha captained the side for the second friendly and scored a penalty in an entertaining first half that finished 2-2.

However, he also slipped right before half-time and was down for a little while which is potentially how he sustained the injury.

All at Barcelona will be crossing their fingers and hoping that Raphinha has not suffered any kind of injury that will see him sidelined.

The Brazilian has been in sensational form for Barcelona in the early weeks of the season, scoring 14 goals in all competitions and leading by example for Hansi Flick's side.

title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse
description: The 49-year-old was found guilty of two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010.
fullText:
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been jailed for seven years after being convicted of child sexual abuse.

Judge Lord Harrower said Dott robbed his victims of "a significant part of their childhood" and said his behaviour bore the hallmarks of grooming.

Dott had denied two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010 but was found guilty following a trial at the High Court in Glasgow.

The 49-year-old Scot, who won the world snooker title in 2006, showed no emotion as he was sentenced, only nodding to someone in the public gallery as he was led away.

Lord Harrower told the High Court in Edinburgh that each of Dott's victims were vulnerable for reasons beyond their age.

He said Dott rewarded the victims with treats and disguised his abuse as being part of a game.

The former snooker champion warned his victims - aged nine and eight when the abuse began - they would not be believed if they told anyone about his actions.

As it happened: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott sentenced

The judge added Dott's victims had experienced "overwhelming emotions of fear, shame and anger" as a result of the abuse, affecting their mental health into adulthood.

Dott's behaviour towards the children "involved a gross violation of trust".

As Lord Harrower addressed him, Dott repeatedly shook his head in apparent disbelief.

The judge added social work reports have deemed Dott poses a "below average risk of reoffending", but as he still maintains his innocence, Lord Harrower could not take into account any remorse from Dott.

The court also heard that Dott has already been the subject of threats in prison, and moved to a different jail as a result.

Euan Dow, representing Dott, told the court the father-of-two was now separated from his wife but "continues to enjoy the support of his family and friends".

He added Dott suffers from "long-standing mental health issues" and that his personal and professional reputations had been destroyed.

The sentence of seven years has been backdated to 24 August, which is when the 49-year-old was remanded in custody.

He will spend the rest of his life on the sex offenders register.

Procurator Fiscal Faye Cook, of the Crown Office, said: "Graeme Dott achieved success and public admiration but, in private, he exploited the trust of two children to abuse and coerce them.

"Dott's criminal behaviour has been his downfall and he now faces the consequences of his actions."

She added that "justice has no time limit" and encouraged any victims of historical abuse to report it.

During the trial, the court heard that Dott had exposed himself and inappropriately touched a primary school girl in the 1990s and attacked a young boy between 2006 and 2010.

Dott called the allegations made against him "disgusting".

The girl, now a woman in her 40s, said Dott had "caressed" her bottom while giving her a piggyback and that, on another occasion, he had exposed himself to her.

On another occasion, she said Dott, of Glasgow, suggested she "take her trousers down" and lifted her top and began kissing her stomach after asking if she wanted to "play a guessing game".

The victim said Dott would kiss her, touch her inappropriately and carried out a sexual act that would, if committed now, amount to rape.

She said she recalled the "smell" of creams Dott used for a skin condition after he kissed her and that the actions left her "shocked and scared".

The court heard that Dott bought her a teddy bear with a love heart on it in the course of the abuse.

Police previously contacted Dott about the allegations in 2001, but no charges were brought.

The woman gave a new statement to police in 2025.

During his evidence, Dott's male victim said the abuse began shortly after Dott defeated Peter Ebdon to win his sole world title at The Crucible in Sheffield in 2006.

The boy, now a man in his 20s, said he was about eight years old when Dott molested him in a shower at a home in South Lanarkshire.

He told the court that Dott "rewarded" him with crisps and fizzy drinks and once handed him a £50 note, only to accuse the boy of stealing it when his parents found out he had the money.

He also said he was abused in a car on a number of occasions and "inappropriately touched" while Dott played online poker.

Dott was convicted of lewd and libidinous practices, which refer to any sexual crimes against children committed prior to 1 December 2010.

The offence was abolished in 2009, but is still used for crimes carried out before then.

Following his conviction in August, the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association said it had permanently revoked Dott's membership with immediate effect.

Dott was previously suspended from all professional snooker activities on 9 April 2025 pending the outcome of his trial.

He was subsequently relegated from the professional ranking list at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season.

Dott has two previous convictions for minor road traffic offences in 2013 and 2015.
